metadata.title: No Default Winner.
metadata.greeting_note: hello lexicon: Ciao (Italian), one word — fresh for this channel (Kumusta, Sawubona, Hej, Merhaba, Jambo, Vanakkam, Annyeong, Sawadee, Hola spent). IN-FOR-BEAR LAW, Yatra form: Bella is the stand-in voice; B00 and outro say so.
metadata.color_semantics: Fidelity claude palette. ONE terracotta event per beat, and it always marks WHERE THE HUMAN DEFAULT BREAKS — the strike through 'wins by default', the younger cohort, the mismatch, the level pivot, the second voice, the agent joining the call. Sources always muted ink.
metadata.note: ILLUSTRATE LAW: Claude UI at B00, B04 (ask, resolved by B05), B10, B11, B12. Body beats are purpose-built Ctr* scenes (CustomerTrust.tsx). SOURCING: five figures, all Capacity, October 2026, rendered verbatim with a separate numeric `bar`. 'Equally likely' has NO number and none is drawn — CtrScale has no numeric prop. No remainder is ever captioned. 'Companies haven't caught up' is labelled interpretation on screen (B06 note, B09 falsifier).
metadata.derived_from: fresh build — new data explainer; all eight body scenes are new components (Ctr* family)

beats.narration_text: Hello, this is Bella, in for Yatra. When an AI tool and a company's own rep give you different answers, who do you believe? It used to be obvious. It isn't anymore.

show.event: Cream page, serif greeting 'Ciao, Bella'; footer chip @Yatra
The ask types itself in
Terracotta send arms
Three result lines stagger in — the ask lands ANSWERED

props.command: When an AI tool and a company's human rep give a customer different answers, who does the customer believe? Walk me through what the latest survey found. Cite every figure on screen and add none of your own.
output: use: 35% of consumers have used an AI agent for customer service
conflict: 44% say an AI tool contradicted a rep or a policy
trust: equally likely to believe either one

beats.narration_text: In one breath: we assumed people trust a human over a machine by default. A new survey says that default is gone. When the two disagree, it's a tie. That's a quiet shift in how brand trust works.

show.event: The old assumption sets in ink serif: 'The human wins by default.'
On 'that default is gone', a terracotta strike draws through 'wins by default'
The replacement types in beneath, in terracotta: 'is one of two answers'
Closer lands

data.slideMeta: The whole story, before any figure
data.closer: A quiet shift in how brand trust works.

beats.narration_text: Start with use. Capacity found thirty-five percent of consumers have used an AI agent for a customer service request at least once. Among Gen Z and Millennials, it's forty-nine percent.

show.event: Row one: 'All consumers' — its bar fills to 35 as the figure sets verbatim: 35%
Row two: 'Gen Z and Millennials' — bar fills to 49 in TERRACOTTA, figure 49%
Source line + note

data.title: At least once

beats.narration_text: And those agents don't always agree with the company. Forty-four percent of consumers say an AI tool has contradicted something a company rep, or a company policy, told them. Two sources, two answers.

Right bubble draws: the AI tool — placeholder answer lines
A terracotta 'does not match' mark lands between them
The figure sets verbatim: 44% with its label

beats.narration_text: So who wins that argument? I asked for the moment itself to be drawn.

show.event: Composer returns with the generation prompt
Terracotta send arms
Running indicator 'drawing the scale…' — result is the next beat

props.command: Draw the moment a customer hears two different answers — one from the company's rep, one from an AI — as a balance scale. Use only what the survey found: consumers are equally likely to trust either one. No numbers.

beats.narration_text: Here it is. The rep on one side, the AI on the other. And the scale doesn't tip. Capacity found consumers are equally likely to trust either one. The human doesn't win by default.

show.event: A balance scale draws; the two pans fill with their labels
The beam rocks — toward the rep, then toward the AI — as if deciding
On 'doesn't tip', it settles dead LEVEL; the pivot lights terracotta

data.verdict: Equally likely to trust either one.

beats.act: THE SHIFT — the tiebreaker is gone
beats.narration_text: That's the shift. A company's rep used to be the final word — the tiebreaker. Now the customer arrives with a second opinion that carries the same weight. The brand's voice is one answer out of two.

show.event: BEFORE panel: a single large 'company's answer' block, crowned 'the final word'
NOW panel: the same block, with a second equal block — 'the customer's AI' — sliding in beside it in TERRACOTTA outline
The crown label is replaced: 'one answer out of two'
Note: this is interpretation, not a figure

data.note: Our read of the finding — not a survey figure.

beats.narration_text: It's changing how people ask, too. Thirty-four percent say they now ask more specific questions because of AI. Customers are arriving better prepared.

show.event: A wide, soft-edged question bubble sets: 'a broad question'
It narrows and sharpens into a tight bubble with crisp edges and a pointer — 'a specific question'
The figure sets verbatim: 34%
Caption + source

beats.narration_text: And some want the AI in the room. Twenty-one percent say they'd let their own AI agent connect them to a human rep — and then join that call itself. Customer, rep, and the customer's AI, on one line.

The agent draws a line to the rep — 'connects them' — and the customer joins
On 'join that call itself', the agent's own line lights TERRACOTTA: three parties on one line
Figure sets verbatim: 21%

beats.narration_text: To be exact: these figures are what consumers report about themselves. The survey doesn't say which answer was right when the two clashed. And that most companies haven't caught up — that's my read, not a finding.

Right column NOT FOUND, headed in terracotta: three items with open boxes
Provenance line

beats.narration_text: So — no default winner. A third of consumers have used AI for customer service; nearly half of younger ones. Forty-four percent have been contradicted by one. And when the AI and the rep disagree, trust splits evenly. Brands are now competing with the customer's own AI for the last word.

The read

artifactLines: Use: 35% of consumers have used an AI agent for a customer service request at least once — 49% among Gen Z and Millennials (Capacity, Oct 2026).
Conflict: 44% say an AI tool has contradicted a company representative or policy (Capacity, Oct 2026).
Trust: when AI and a human rep conflict, consumers are equally likely to trust either — not automatically the human (Capacity, Oct 2026).
Behaviour: 34% ask more specific questions because of AI; 21% would let their own AI agent connect them to a rep and join the call (Capacity, Oct 2026).
The read: the rep is no longer the tiebreaker — brands now share the last word with the customer's AI.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. If you run customer service, paste this: Customers sometimes get a different answer from an AI tool than from our reps, and they're as likely to believe the AI. Find the parts of our policy that are easiest to misread, and draft what a rep should say when a customer says the AI told them otherwise. Watch whether it fixes the policy, not just the script.
